name: param-uq-02-observables
title: Multi-observable robustness — basal_elongation_rate dominates MASS; growth-rate ranking is window-dependent
claim:
Over a longer (360-step) window the MASS observables become responsive, and
basal_elongation_rate DOMINATES them — total-order Sobol ≈ 0.86 for both
dry_mass and cell_mass — confirming and extending the param-uq-01 finding to
mass. For instantaneous growth rate, however, the ranking is WINDOW-DEPENDENT:
ppGpp-synthesis kS edges basal_elongation_rate at 360 steps (0.62 vs 0.51), vs
basal's 0.97 at 120 steps. So the dominant driver of growth-rate variance shifts
with the integration window — a genuine nuance on top of the headline result.
question:
Over a longer (360-step) window, do dry_mass and cell_mass become responsive to
the 3 effective elongation knobs, does basal_elongation_rate remain dominant
across observables, and is the ranking stable to the choice of observable/window?

report.title: param-uq-02-observables — multi-observable elongation sensitivity (360-step)
report.evidence_quality: order-2 PCE, n=24+8, 2 seeds, per-observable; mass-fit test rel-err ~0%, igr ~2%
report.objective:
Test whether the param-uq-01 finding (basal_elongation_rate dominates
instantaneous_growth_rate at 120 steps) generalises to MASS observables
(dry_mass, cell_mass) when the window is extended to 360 steps (~13% of a
generation), and whether the ranking is stable to observable/window choice.
report.setup:
Same 3 effective knobs (from param-uq-00-screen):
  - basal_elongation_rate          [15, 28]   aa/s   (translation)
  - kS                             [60, 140]         (ppGpp/charging kinetics)
  - chrom.basal_elongation_rate    [700, 1200] nt/s  (DNA-pol)
Window: 360 simulation steps. Observables: dry_mass, cell_mass,
instantaneous_growth_rate. Budget: n=24 train + 8 test, 2 PCRV seeds.
Per-observable order-2 PCE → analytic Sobol. Fresh initial_state per sample
(v2ecoli PR #197). Reproducer: pbg-uq examples/v2ecoli_uq_observables.py.
report.result:
Per-observable total-order Sobol (mean across 2 seeds):

| Observable | basal_elongation_rate | kS | DNA-pol rate | dominant | test rel-err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dry_mass   | **0.863** | 0.142 | 0.043 | basal_elongation_rate | ~0.0% |
| cell_mass  | **0.867** | 0.137 | 0.042 | basal_elongation_rate | ~0.0% |
| growth_rate (360 steps) | 0.511 | **0.615** | 0.123 | **kS** | ~2% |

- MASS observables now respond (vs <0.16% at 120 steps) and
  basal_elongation_rate dominates them (~0.86) with a near-exact surrogate fit.
- For instantaneous growth rate at 360 steps, kS (0.615) edges
  basal_elongation_rate (0.511) — a reversal from the 120-step result (basal
  0.97). The growth-rate ranking is window-dependent.
report.interpretation:
The headline finding HOLDS and STRENGTHENS for the mass observables: ribosome
basal elongation rate is the dominant driver of dry_mass and cell_mass variance
over a window long enough for mass to accumulate (Sobol ≈ 0.86, near-exact fit).
This is the expected biology — faster elongation → more protein → more mass.

The interesting nuance is on instantaneous growth rate: its sensitivity ranking
DEPENDS ON THE INTEGRATION WINDOW. At 120 steps basal_elongation_rate dominates
(0.97); at 360 steps the ppGpp/charging constant kS catches up and slightly
exceeds it (0.62 vs 0.51). Mechanistically plausible — a short window captures
the immediate elongation-speed effect, while a longer window lets the
ppGpp/charging regulation (kS) shape the realised growth rate. Practically: a
growth-rate sensitivity ranking should always state its window; mass is the more
window-robust readout of elongation sensitivity. (A minor ill-conditioning
warning appeared for the weak kS/DNA-pol basis columns; it does not affect the
dominant mass result, whose fit error is ~0%.)
report.decision:
PASS — basal_elongation_rate dominance generalises to the MASS observables
(Sobol ≈ 0.86, robust). KEY DISCOVERY: the growth-rate ranking is
window-dependent (kS overtakes basal by 360 steps), so growth-rate Sobol must be
reported with its window. This motivates param-uq-03 (growth-stratified /
cell-cycle-resolved sensitivity) to map how the ranking evolves over time.

assumptions.text:
360 steps is enough for dry_mass/cell_mass to accumulate a detectable response
to elongation-rate perturbations. CONFIRMED: mass fit errors ~0% with a clear
basal_elongation_rate signal (vs <0.16% response at 120 steps).

A growth-rate sensitivity ranking is window-independent. REFUTED: the igr
dominant knob flips from basal_elongation_rate (120 steps) to kS (360 steps).

tests.name: basal-dominates-mass-observables
tests.question:
Does basal_elongation_rate dominate (total-order Sobol > 0.5) the mass
observables (dry_mass, cell_mass) over the 360-step window?

measure.detail:
basal_elongation_rate total-order Sobol = 0.863 (dry_mass) and 0.867
(cell_mass), dominant for both; surrogate test rel-err ~0%.

tests.cites_note: Sobol > 0.5 is a methodological dominance threshold; not literature-derived.

tests.name: growth-rate-ranking-is-window-dependent
tests.question:
Does the dominant driver of instantaneous-growth-rate variance change between
the 120-step and 360-step windows — i.e. is the growth-rate ranking
window-dependent, as this study claims?

measure.detail:
CONFIRMED window-dependence — the igr dominant knob flips: basal_elongation_rate
(Sobol 0.97 @ 120 steps) → kS (0.615, edging basal's 0.511) @ 360 steps.
measured_value = fraction of the compared window pairs that show a DIFFERENT igr
dominant driver = 1.0 (the single 120↔360 pair differs). This is the study's
headline discovery, framed affirmatively (the window-independence hypothesis is
refuted; see assumptions).

tests.cites_note: Window-dependence detection threshold is methodological; not literature-derived.

growth-rate-ranking-is-window-dependent.detail: Window-dependence CONFIRMED: igr dominant flips basal (0.97 @120) -> kS (0.615 @360). The study's headline discovery.

if_primary_tests_pass.interpretation:
basal_elongation_rate dominance generalises to the MASS observables over a
360-step window (total-order Sobol ≈ 0.86 for both dry_mass and cell_mass,
near-exact surrogate fit) — confirming and strengthening param-uq-01. The
companion finding is that the instantaneous-growth-rate ranking is
window-dependent: kS (0.615) overtakes basal_elongation_rate (0.511) at 360
steps, vs basal's 0.97 at 120 steps. So a growth-rate Sobol ranking must always
state its integration window; mass is the more window-robust readout.
pipeline_unblocks: param-uq-03-growth-stratified maps how the ranking evolves across the cell cycle.

diagnose: If mass observables did not respond at 360 steps, the window is still too short for mass to accumulate signal — extend toward a full generation (~2760 steps).
The minor ill-conditioning warning on the weak kS/DNA-pol basis columns does not affect the dominant mass result (fit err ~0%); revisit only if the mass ranking destabilises.
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: Without a robust mass result the cell-cycle-stratified study has no anchor.

study_card.goal:
Test whether the param-uq-01 finding (basal_elongation_rate dominates igr at 120
steps) generalises to the MASS observables (dry_mass, cell_mass) at a longer
360-step window, and whether the ranking is stable to observable/window choice.
study_card.why_before_next:
Confirming mass dominance and discovering that the growth-rate ranking is
window-dependent motivates the cell-cycle-stratified study (param-uq-03), which
resolves how the ranking evolves over time.

biological_summary:
Over a window long enough for mass to accumulate, faster ribosome elongation yields
more protein and more mass — so basal_elongation_rate dominates dry_mass and
cell_mass variance (Sobol ≈ 0.86). Instantaneous growth rate is more subtle: a short
window captures the immediate elongation-speed effect, while a longer window lets the
ppGpp/charging regulation (kS) shape the realised growth rate, so kS catches up to
and slightly exceeds basal_elongation_rate by 360 steps.

literature_anchors.expectation:
Faster ribosome elongation increases protein-synthesis flux and biomass; the
v2ecoli baseline elongation parameterization derives from the wcEcoli model.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — mass rises with elongation rate; Sobol ≈ 0.86.

model_change.notes:

implementation_requirements.description:
examples/v2ecoli_uq_observables.py: n=24+8 PCRV per seed (2 seeds), 360-step
window, fresh initial_state per sample, per-observable order-2 PCE → analytic Sobol
for dry_mass, cell_mass, instantaneous_growth_rate.

design_pivot_required.question: Can a growth-rate sensitivity ranking be reported window-agnostically?
design_pivot_required.decision:
NO. The igr dominant driver flips between the 120- and 360-step windows, so any
growth-rate Sobol ranking must state its integration window. Mass observables are
the window-robust readout and are preferred for headline elongation-sensitivity claims.
alternatives: Report a single window-agnostic growth-rate ranking (rejected — the ranking is window-dependent).

robustness.swept_param: ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.basal_elongation_rate (+ ppGpp kS, chromosome basal_elongation_rate), per-observable PCE

falsifiability:
The mass-dominance claim fails if a longer/shorter integration window or a
held-out PCRV seed reorders the per-observable Sobol ranking for the mass
observables. The companion growth-rate ranking IS already shown to be
window-dependent (kS overtakes basal_elongation_rate by 360 steps), which both
bounds the claim and demonstrates the test can discriminate.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: basal_elongation_rate dominates every observable uniformly, at any integration window.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: Per-observable Sobol across windows — mass dominance holds (~0.86) but the growth-rate ranking is window-dependent (kS overtakes basal_elongation_rate by 360 steps), so dominance is observable- and window-specific.
